summary:
Partition 2 (Sources, Clarification, Visual Editor Drawer, Quality/Feedback and the React Flow canvas) has no CRITICAL or MAJOR defects. None of the changes touch Python core models or the Graph A RFC 8785 serialization path, so SHA-256 stability is not at risk from this diff. The ONT-EVO-001 guards in the pure `validateConceptEdit` function are correct and well tested. They block rename, archetype change, reparenting (including adding a parent to a root concept), clearing or changing the committed target hub, removing the committed definition, removing committed synonyms, attributes or mappings, changing a committed attribute's data type, and making an optional attribute mandatory. Cycle detection under ONT-DAG-001 handles both self-parenting and multi-hop cycles. Source uploads read raw bytes through `arrayBuffer()`, and the canvas has deletion turned off.

There are 10 MINOR findings:
- **Drawer state:** the drawer keeps its form and change-detection snapshot when the selection is cleared outside the drawer.
- **Spurious save:** the 'nothing changed' check treats null and undefined as different, so saving an unchanged concept still writes to the store.
- **Change detection:** the concurrent-edit check runs only in the browser and compares `JSON.stringify` output, which is fragile.
- **Parent URIs:** a concept can point to a parent that does not exist.
- **Quality panel:** after a session switch, the form can be filled from the previous session's scorecard.
- **Grounding gauge:** the bar colour uses the unrounded value, which does not match the rounding the notes claim.
- **Clarification panel:** local drafts carry over between sessions.
- **Sources panel:** a failed upload that returns null is not reported as an error.
- **Canvas:** auto-layout on session switch depends on the order in which the store updates.
- **Tests:** the component tests only render static markup. They never exercise the save, cancel, upload or waiver behaviour that the notes say was fixed.

The verdict is PASS because there are no CRITICAL or MAJOR findings.

findings.title: Drawer keeps stale form and change-detection snapshot when the selection is cleared outside the drawer
findings.description: `prevSelectedUriRef` and `initialSnapshotRef` are only reset in `handleClose`. If `selectedNodeId` is cleared any other way (session switch, store reset, another caller of `selectNode(null)`), the component returns null but keeps the old URI and form state. When the same concept URI is selected again, which is common across sessions or versions of the same ontology, the load effect does not run. The user then sees the previous unsaved edits. Either every save fails with `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION_DETECTED` (because the snapshot is stale), or the old session's edits can be saved into the new session when the two concepts are byte-identical. This contradicts the claimed MIN-01 fix ('reopening the same concept re-initializes cleanly'). Closing and reopening the drawer works around it.
findings.recommendation: Reset `prevSelectedUriRef` and `initialSnapshotRef` whenever `selectedConcept` becomes undefined, and include the active session ID in the reset key (for example, compare `${sessionId}|${uri}`). Alternatively, have the parent key the drawer by session and URI so React remounts it.

findings.title: No-op check treats null and undefined as different; a cast hides undefined in the required `definition` field
findings.description: `updated` turns empty fields into `undefined`, but the store can hold `null` (the tests use `target_hub: null` and `parent_concept_uri: null`) or `""`. Saving an unchanged concept then fails `currentStoreConcept.target_hub === updated.target_hub`, so `updateConcept` still runs and marks the draft as changed. This contradicts the claim that an unchanged save skips the store write. Separately, `definition: (updatedDef as unknown as string)` places `undefined` in a field typed as a required `string`, which bypasses strict typing. A cleared definition on an uncommitted concept can then reach the backend as missing.
findings.recommendation: Normalise both sides before comparing (for example `norm = (v) => (v == null || v === '' ? undefined : v)`). Either make `ConceptNode.definition` optional in `types.ts`, or block saving an empty definition, instead of using the double cast.

findings.title: Concurrent-edit detection runs only in the browser and compares `JSON.stringify` output
findings.description: Conflicts are detected by comparing `JSON.stringify(currentStoreConcept)` with a snapshot. After a successful save, the snapshot is set to `JSON.stringify(updated)`, not to what the store actually holds. If `updateConcept` changes the object in any way (extra fields, a timestamp, different key order), every later save in the same open drawer reports a false conflict. In addition, `updateConcept(uri, updated)` is called without a base revision or ETag. As a result, ONT-EVO-003 is only enforced against changes in the local store, not against other server-side writers, unless the store adds a revision itself (that code is in another partition).
findings.recommendation: After saving, re-read the snapshot from the store (`getState().nodes`). Better, use a server revision/version or CAS hash on each concept and pass it to `updateConcept` as the OCC precondition (If-Match).

findings.title: Parent concept URI is not checked for existence, and the strict regex may reject existing URIs
findings.description: `validateConceptEdit` checks the URN pattern and cycles but never confirms that `parent_concept_uri` matches a concept in `allNodes`. A user can therefore set a parent that points to nothing. Also, the regex `^urn:(ontology:entity|opendv:concept):[a-z0-9_]+$` runs on every save. Any concept whose already-committed parent URI uses a different but valid form (uppercase, hyphens) could never be saved.
findings.recommendation: Report a `PARENT_NOT_FOUND` error when the parent is missing from `allNodes`. Apply the format regex only when the parent value has changed from the committed one.

findings.title: Quality panel can fill the new session's form from the previous session's scorecard
findings.description: The session-change effect runs as soon as `activeSessionId` changes, and at that moment `qualityScorecard` is usually still the previous session's. The form is filled with that stale rating, comment and rationale. When the new scorecard arrives, nothing re-syncs it because `prevSessionIdRef` already matches. The waiver effect only reacts to waiver_applied going from false to true. If it was true in both sessions, the new session's rationale is never loaded.
findings.recommendation: Tie the scorecard to its session (for example a `qualityScorecard.session_id` field) and re-seed the form only when the scorecard's session matches the active session and differs from the last one used to seed it.

findings.title: Grounding gauge colour uses the unrounded value, and the sub-count comes from a different source
findings.description: The notes say the bar colour follows `Math.round(groundingPct) >= 65`, but the code uses the raw `groundingPct >= 65.0`. A value of 64.6 is displayed as '65%' with a red (failing) bar. Using the raw value is the correct contract check (>= 0.6500), so the problem is the mismatched display and notes. Also, the percentage comes from `qualityScorecard.grounding_score` while the sub-label `(grounded/total)` is counted from local nodes, so the two can contradict each other.
findings.recommendation: Show the percentage with enough precision (for example `toFixed(1)`) or floor it, so the label and colour agree with the 0.65 threshold. Label the local count as separate from the server score.

findings.title: Clarification drafts and errors carry over between sessions; the answer payload has no OCC precondition
findings.description: `activeDrafts` and `submissionErrors` are local state keyed only by `question_id` and are never cleared when `activeSession` changes. If question IDs repeat across sessions, stale selections appear. `ClarificationAnswer` carries no expected version, so the header's 'Optimistic locking / OCC answer submission' claim relies entirely on the store. Any `false` returned by `submitAnswer` is labelled as an ONT-EVO-003 conflict, even when the cause is something else (validation, network).
findings.recommendation: Clear the local drafts and errors when the session ID changes. Send a question or session revision with each answer, and have `submitAnswer` return a typed result so the real failure reason is shown.

findings.title: Sources panel misses failed uploads that return null; one store value is unused; sources can be deleted during parsing
findings.description: `handleFiles` only records an error when `uploadSource` throws. If it returns null or undefined (a failure), the file is silently skipped, which undermines the 'collects all file errors' claim. `isLoadingSources` is subscribed but never used. Delete buttons stay enabled while `parsingState.status === 'parsing'`, so a source can be removed while a parse job is still using it.
findings.recommendation: Treat a falsy `uploaded` value as an error, either use or remove `isLoadingSources`, and disable deletion while a parse is running.

findings.title: Component tests only render static markup; the claimed behaviour fixes are never exercised
findings.description: All component tests use `renderToStaticMarkup`. Nothing tests `handleSave` (raw draft building, concurrent-edit detection, the unchanged-save path), cancel/reset, the upload size guard (413) and batch error collection, the parse session guard, waiver submission and key clearing, or answer-rejection banners. 'VisualEditorDrawer renders concept details and handles validation' only checks rendering. 'allows removing uncommitted draft values on committed concept' sets null on both sides, so nothing is actually removed. `validateConceptEdit` itself is well covered.
findings.recommendation: Add interactive tests (happy-dom with @testing-library/react under Bun) for drawer save and cancel, concurrent-edit detection, the unchanged-save path with null fields, the upload size guard, and waiver key clearing. Fix the 'removing uncommitted values' test so the draft actually clears a value the committed concept does not have.

findings.title: Auto-layout on session switch depends on store update order; a failed layout leaves the canvas empty
findings.description: On a session switch, `setNodes([])` runs after the position-sync effect, and the auto-layout is the only thing that repopulates the canvas. If `activeSession` changes before `nodes` in the store, the layout runs on the previous session's nodes and sets `hasAutoLaidOutRef = true`. The new session's nodes then fall back to the staggered grid and never get an automatic layout. If `layoutGraph` rejects, the nodes stay `[]` until `initialFlowNodes` changes again.
findings.recommendation: Run the first layout once the nodes for the new session are present (for example, check that the nodes belong to the session, or reset the flag whenever the set of node IDs changes). In the catch branch, fall back to `setNodes(initialFlowNodes)`.

findings.title: Fit the view after auto-layout
findings.description: `fitView` only applies when the canvas first mounts. Nodes placed later by the async layout or on a session switch can end up off-screen.
findings.recommendation: Call `useReactFlow().fitView()` after the layout results are applied.

findings.title: Keep React Flow's internal node fields when syncing
findings.description: The sync effect rebuilds each node from `fn`, which drops React Flow's internal fields (`measured`, `selected`, `dragging`). This can cause re-measuring and flicker on every search keystroke or selection change.
findings.recommendation: Merge as `{ ...prevNode, ...fn, position: existingPos }` when a previous node exists.

findings.title: Check external mapping URI format
findings.description: Mapping target URIs are free text with no CURIE or IRI check for the chosen scheme.
findings.recommendation: Add a CURIE/IRI pattern check for each scheme, or rely on server-side grounding checks and show their result.

positive_highlights: `validateConceptEdit` is a pure, exported function that enforces the ONT-EVO-001 rules (no rename, archetype change or reparenting, committed target hub and definition kept, committed synonyms, attributes and mappings kept, attribute data types frozen, optional attributes cannot become mandatory), and focused unit tests cover these rules.
ONT-DAG-001 cycle detection walks the parent chain with a visited set, catching both self-parenting and multi-hop cycles without looping forever.
Source uploads use `file.arrayBuffer()` for exact bytes, and size and MIME checks run before the file is read into memory, reported as RFC 7807-style toasts.
`deleteKeyCode={null}` prevents canvas deletions that would bypass the store; a layout generation counter and session ID ref prevent results from an outdated layout being applied.
No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; all user and LLM-supplied text is rendered through React's escaping. The waiver key uses a password input and is cleared on success and on session switch.
Async handlers catch and report their errors, so there are no unhandled promise rejections in the upload, delete, parse, answer or waiver paths.

findings.title: Concurrent-edit detection runs only in the browser and compares `JSON.stringify` output
findings.description: Conflicts are detected by comparing `JSON.stringify(currentStoreConcept)` with a snapshot. After a successful save, the snapshot is set to `JSON.stringify(updated)`, not to what the store actually holds. If `updateConcept` changes the object in any way (extra fields, a timestamp, different key order), every later save in the same open drawer reports a false conflict. In addition, `updateConcept(uri, updated)` is called without a base revision or ETag. As a result, ONT-EVO-003 is only enforced against changes in the local store, not against other server-side writers, unless the store adds a revision itself (that code is in another partition).
findings.recommendation: After saving, re-read the snapshot from the store (`getState().nodes`). Better, use a server revision/version or CAS hash on each concept and pass it to `updateConcept` as the OCC precondition (If-Match).

findings.title: Parent concept URI is not checked for existence, and the strict regex may reject existing URIs
findings.description: `validateConceptEdit` checks the URN pattern and cycles but never confirms that `parent_concept_uri` matches a concept in `allNodes`. A user can therefore set a parent that points to nothing. Also, the regex `^urn:(ontology:entity|opendv:concept):[a-z0-9_]+$` runs on every save. Any concept whose already-committed parent URI uses a different but valid form (uppercase, hyphens) could never be saved.
findings.recommendation: Report a `PARENT_NOT_FOUND` error when the parent is missing from `allNodes`. Apply the format regex only when the parent value has changed from the committed one.

findings.title: Quality panel can fill the new session's form from the previous session's scorecard
findings.description: The session-change effect runs as soon as `activeSessionId` changes, and at that moment `qualityScorecard` is usually still the previous session's. The form is filled with that stale rating, comment and rationale. When the new scorecard arrives, nothing re-syncs it because `prevSessionIdRef` already matches. The waiver effect only reacts to waiver_applied going from false to true. If it was true in both sessions, the new session's rationale is never loaded.
findings.recommendation: Tie the scorecard to its session (for example a `qualityScorecard.session_id` field) and re-seed the form only when the scorecard's session matches the active session and differs from the last one used to seed it.

findings.title: Grounding gauge colour uses the unrounded value, and the sub-count comes from a different source
findings.description: The notes say the bar colour follows `Math.round(groundingPct) >= 65`, but the code uses the raw `groundingPct >= 65.0`. A value of 64.6 is displayed as '65%' with a red (failing) bar. Using the raw value is the correct contract check (>= 0.6500), so the problem is the mismatched display and notes. Also, the percentage comes from `qualityScorecard.grounding_score` while the sub-label `(grounded/total)` is counted from local nodes, so the two can contradict each other.
findings.recommendation: Show the percentage with enough precision (for example `toFixed(1)`) or floor it, so the label and colour agree with the 0.65 threshold. Label the local count as separate from the server score.

findings.title: Clarification drafts and errors carry over between sessions; the answer payload has no OCC precondition
findings.description: `activeDrafts` and `submissionErrors` are local state keyed only by `question_id` and are never cleared when `activeSession` changes. If question IDs repeat across sessions, stale selections appear. `ClarificationAnswer` carries no expected version, so the header's 'Optimistic locking / OCC answer submission' claim relies entirely on the store. Any `false` returned by `submitAnswer` is labelled as an ONT-EVO-003 conflict, even when the cause is something else (validation, network).
findings.recommendation: Clear the local drafts and errors when the session ID changes. Send a question or session revision with each answer, and have `submitAnswer` return a typed result so the real failure reason is shown.

findings.title: Sources panel misses failed uploads that return null; one store value is unused; sources can be deleted during parsing
findings.description: `handleFiles` only records an error when `uploadSource` throws. If it returns null or undefined (a failure), the file is silently skipped, which undermines the 'collects all file errors' claim. `isLoadingSources` is subscribed but never used. Delete buttons stay enabled while `parsingState.status === 'parsing'`, so a source can be removed while a parse job is still using it.
findings.recommendation: Treat a falsy `uploaded` value as an error, either use or remove `isLoadingSources`, and disable deletion while a parse is running.

findings.title: Component tests only render static markup; the claimed behaviour fixes are never exercised
findings.description: All component tests use `renderToStaticMarkup`. Nothing tests `handleSave` (raw draft building, concurrent-edit detection, the unchanged-save path), cancel/reset, the upload size guard (413) and batch error collection, the parse session guard, waiver submission and key clearing, or answer-rejection banners. 'VisualEditorDrawer renders concept details and handles validation' only checks rendering. 'allows removing uncommitted draft values on committed concept' sets null on both sides, so nothing is actually removed. `validateConceptEdit` itself is well covered.
findings.recommendation: Add interactive tests (happy-dom with @testing-library/react under Bun) for drawer save and cancel, concurrent-edit detection, the unchanged-save path with null fields, the upload size guard, and waiver key clearing. Fix the 'removing uncommitted values' test so the draft actually clears a value the committed concept does not have.

findings.title: Auto-layout on session switch depends on store update order; a failed layout leaves the canvas empty
findings.description: On a session switch, `setNodes([])` runs after the position-sync effect, and the auto-layout is the only thing that repopulates the canvas. If `activeSession` changes before `nodes` in the store, the layout runs on the previous session's nodes and sets `hasAutoLaidOutRef = true`. The new session's nodes then fall back to the staggered grid and never get an automatic layout. If `layoutGraph` rejects, the nodes stay `[]` until `initialFlowNodes` changes again.
findings.recommendation: Run the first layout once the nodes for the new session are present (for example, check that the nodes belong to the session, or reset the flag whenever the set of node IDs changes). In the catch branch, fall back to `setNodes(initialFlowNodes)`.

findings.title: Fit the view after auto-layout
findings.description: `fitView` only applies when the canvas first mounts. Nodes placed later by the async layout or on a session switch can end up off-screen.
findings.recommendation: Call `useReactFlow().fitView()` after the layout results are applied.

findings.title: Keep React Flow's internal node fields when syncing
findings.description: The sync effect rebuilds each node from `fn`, which drops React Flow's internal fields (`measured`, `selected`, `dragging`). This can cause re-measuring and flicker on every search keystroke or selection change.
findings.recommendation: Merge as `{ ...prevNode, ...fn, position: existingPos }` when a previous node exists.

findings.title: Check external mapping URI format
findings.description: Mapping target URIs are free text with no CURIE or IRI check for the chosen scheme.
findings.recommendation: Add a CURIE/IRI pattern check for each scheme, or rely on server-side grounding checks and show their result.

positive_highlights: `validateConceptEdit` is a pure, exported function that enforces the ONT-EVO-001 rules (no rename, archetype change or reparenting, committed target hub and definition kept, committed synonyms, attributes and mappings kept, attribute data types frozen, optional attributes cannot become mandatory), and focused unit tests cover these rules.
ONT-DAG-001 cycle detection walks the parent chain with a visited set, catching both self-parenting and multi-hop cycles without looping forever.
Source uploads use `file.arrayBuffer()` for exact bytes, and size and MIME checks run before the file is read into memory, reported as RFC 7807-style toasts.
`deleteKeyCode={null}` prevents canvas deletions that would bypass the store; a layout generation counter and session ID ref prevent results from an outdated layout being applied.
No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; all user and LLM-supplied text is rendered through React's escaping. The waiver key uses a password input and is cleared on success and on session switch.
Async handlers catch and report their errors, so there are no unhandled promise rejections in the upload, delete, parse, answer or waiver paths.
